FIX ROUND 432e for issue #432 (part of #330), PROPOSED DECISION 0101: A PERSONAL MAP'S EFFECTIVE IDENTITY KEEPS EVERYTHING ITS SCHEMA VERSION MEANS. This story is docs only. The branch is story-432-personal-config-decision, checked out in this worktree at 58b1567ad (the design story's ca85e89b6 and its reforge round's 58b1567ad, on main bc36e9302). When you are done, the branch is 58b1567ad plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- Design story 432d (design-story-for-issue-432-part--ade6364a) drafted decision 0101, proposed. Its first review returned three MEDIUMs and five LOWs, which the return in 58b1567ad answered. Its second review stopped it at REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD, high, recorded on #432 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/432#issuecomment-6520928038). Keep everything that review did not find wrong: the inventory, options A/B/C, the selection matrix, the path bases and migration, the adapters answer, the stock-map test, the leak rules, the eight rulings' recommendations, the slices, and the index's gap rows for 0097-0100 (the controller reconciles them at restack; do not delete them).

THE OPERATOR'S RULING: 2026-10-30, in chat, "go with recommended" (#432, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/432#issuecomment-6522823412): fix round 432e runs as recommended, the effective identity over the parsed, typed map.

THE FINDING (fix it; nothing else):
1. **HIGH, security (decision 0071 rulings 3 and 9; a proposal that would weaken a refusal): the proposed effective identity drops the schema label, but the label changes what a grant means.**
   - Claim under test: 0101 about :441-455 and ruling 6 discard `schema` from the normalized map as irrelevant, and ruling 7 (about :503-523) compares that effective digest on resume to refuse source drift.
   - Case: two maps identical but for `forge.realms/v7` against `forge.realms/v8`, each with journal `/tmp/shared.db`, realm `private` at `/tmp/repo` on `main`, and capabilities `{"web-search":{"dialect":"search-native","retain":false}}`. The documented normalization gives both 30491a00d2c59591c1fbe72b7129c9ae93b94cb12995c1038fe8f588fb554f75. But crates/brokkr-core/src/realms/grants.rs:186-189 and :232-247 read v7 as Unreserved with a `retain=false` restriction and v8 as Veto without it, and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/capabilities/binding.rs:258-262 and capabilities/dialect.rs:403-420 give them different retention and admission.
   - Expected: different effective identities, and a SourceDrift refusal for a semantics-changing rewrite.
   - **Fix (recommended):** define the effective identity over the PARSED, typed map: every field as the loader reads it under its label, with each grant's typed form (its reservation class, retention and restrictions) rather than its written JSON. Two maps are equivalent only if they parse to the same typed value. If the decision keeps a digest over written JSON for any purpose, it keeps `schema` in it. State which typed value is digested and where its canonical serialization lives (name the existing type and file:line, or say a slice adds one). Re-check every other place 0101 says a field is "irrelevant" to identity the same way: name each field it drops, and cite the loader line that shows the field changes nothing, or keep it.
   - Name the regression cases in slices 3 and 4: the v7/v8 pair above gives two identities and resume refuses with SourceDrift; a key-order-only rewrite of one map gives one identity and resumes; a boundary omitted against `boundary: "namespace"` under a label whose default is namespace gives one identity (core/realms.rs about :414-420), and under a label where omission means something else gives two.
   - Update rulings 6 and 7 and their recommendations to match, and the "what is unmeasured" lines.

NOT THIS ROUND: the chief's LOW about 58b1567ad's trailers (a blank line between `Signed-off-by` and `Co-Authored-By`) is the controller's to fix at restack. Your own commit's trailers must be contiguous: `Signed-off-by` on one line, `Co-Authored-By` on the very next line, no blank line between. The chief's run-integrity note needs no change.

RULES
- Scope: decision 0101 only (and its README row only if its title changes). No code, no test, no guide edit, no change to realms.json, `.gitignore` or any tracked sample. No `$ brokkr` prompt in the decision.
- Ground every claim about today's behaviour in a file:line at HEAD, or in a command you ran and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is "unmeasured", never asserted.
- Touch no contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or the top-level reference/ directory.
- Gates:
  - cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- decisions_index:: doc_truth:: doc_samples:: (timeout 590)
  - typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones; git diff --check
  - TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing; if it is read-only in your box, a fresh directory under /tmp). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.

- Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding, written as a test case: the claim in the decision, the code or command that tests it, and what was observed against what the decision says.

THE REVIEW JUDGES: the story's five judges (every inventory claim true at HEAD; every option stated fairly; nothing proposed weakens a trust, egress, boundary or schema refusal or lets resume pick up a changed local file silently; consistency with #697's ruled shelf; buildable slices with tests), and in particular that no two maps whose loaders read them differently can share an effective identity under 0101's definition.

SIZE (an estimate): about 20 to 60 lines of the decision changed.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- Docs only. Other branches add decisions 0097 (#899), 0099 (#918), 0100 (#431), 0102 (#909) and 0103 (#430); decision 0098 merged with #914. Their README rows union-merge with yours; the controller reconciles the gap rows at restack.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes:
Fixed the HIGH security finding in proposed decision 0101 and committed 1422925fe on story-432-personal-config-decision. The effective identity is now defined over a parsed, typed EffectiveMap rather than written JSON: it carries the schema label as the semantic discriminator, the world journal, provisional_offices, each realm's loader-read fields, and each grant's typed CapabilityGrant (reservation class/retention, tools, offices and parsed restrictions). The normalizer never uses CapabilityGrant::value(), because that rebuilds written JSON and collapses the v7 restriction and v8 veto. Every materialized default is named with the loader line that reads absence and its explicit spelling alike; no other field is called irrelevant. Rulings 6 and 7, their recommendations, the pin/resume text, consequences, and slices 3 and 4 are updated. The v7/v8 identity and SourceDrift regressions, the key-order-only one-identity/resume case, and the boundary omitted-vs-explicit namespace case are named; the future-label case is named with the label that would carry it. A 'what the effective identity does not measure' paragraph records paths, file bytes, dialect restriction judgment, and the unbuilt v15 pin/SourceDrift execution as unmeasured. The schema label is kept in the typed value as the conservative semantic discriminator, so no two maps whose loaders read them differently can share an identity; this also means cross-label maps that happen to read alike need not share one. No code, test, contract, guide, realms.json, .gitignore or sample changed, and the README row was left alone because the title did not change. The controller still owns the chief's LOW about 58b1567ad's trailers; this commit's Signed-off-by and Co-Authored-By are contiguous with the latter last, and git log recognizes the signer.

Evidence run in this session:
- cargo test -p brokkr-core --test it --locked -- realms:: => 4 passed, 0 failed; it includes an_older_grant_keeps_retain_as_a_restriction_and_round_trips_exactly (v6/v7 Unreserved with retain restriction) and a_v8_grant_reads_retain_false_as_the_veto_and_omission_as_inherit (v8 Veto/Inherit).
- Scratch Python of the exact finding case: the old 58b1567ad normalization gave v7 = v8 = 30491a00d2c59591c1fbe72b7129c9ae93b94cb12995c1038fe8f588fb554f75, while the proposed typed form gave v7 e14fc55bb653ee921dabc0e8d22d7e08003c8a1817dbabb5a153991e53dc2b0e and v8 2c5a377fe109a573ad0bde3f9ce76edb1008df103fb6c1e1648fd2a30bfe0532. The same scratch check gave one identity for a key-order-only rewrite and for boundary omitted vs boundary:'namespace' under a namespace-default label, and two when the boundary word changed.

members.adversarial: MEDIUM correctness, decision 0071 rulings 3 and 9: typed equality and the selected canonical serialization disagree on signed floating zero. Claim: decision 0101:453-485 hashes serialized EffectiveMap using canonical::sha256_hex and declares maps equivalent exactly when their typed EffectiveMap values are equal; :567-573 permits equivalent rewrites on resume. Concrete input: two maps with schema forge.realms/v7, journal /tmp/shared.db, realm private at /tmp/repo on main, capabilities {web-search:{dialect:search-native,cost:0.0}}, changing only cost to -0.0. In a git-archive HEAD scratch under /var/tmp, RealmMap::parse accepted both and assert_eq!(positive, negative) passed. A Serialize mirror of the proposed EffectiveGrant (dialect, tools, offices, retention, restrictions) passed through serde_json::to_value and the named canonical serializer retained 0.0 versus -0.0; its digests were 8332db571ffd4f14540b45f2bdfb86288edd530bcfa732b7166a8c0bc121e5c4 versus 74dafcf2a3a7b2b3c92fe3c7a87518b84d20141c7e4844bf718714929b746aa7. The equal-digest assertion failed. Evidence: grants.rs:239-248 preserves restriction Values, canonical.rs:9-21 serializes them unchanged.
